We divide the square into horizontal strips at y = 1/3 and 2/3. Points are placed 4 on the bottom, 3 on the 1/3 line, 2 on the 2/3 line, and 3 on the top. This avoids having 4 points on any single edge. The minimum area arises from the smallest base (length 1/3 along an edge or interior line) multiplied by the smallest height (1/3). Thus, min area = 1/2 * 1/3 * 1/3 = 1/18 ~ 0.0555. To optimize further and increase the minimum area, the spacing between points on the same line is increased to 1/3, while points on adjacent lines are offset to prevent small vertical gaps.
